title: Potato and Pea Samosas with Mint-Coriander Chutney
summary: An oil-rubbed pastry is wrapped round a filling of crushed potatoes and peas with cumin, coriander, turmeric, ginger and chilli, then the samosas are fried slowly until crisp.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
chilled water, plus 1-2 tbsp as needed
floury potatoes (such as russet or Maris Piper), scrubbed
Kashmiri chilli powder (pure chilli) or paprika
fine sea salt or table salt
fresh coriander, leaves and tender stems
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the pastry
steps.text: Rub the oil into the flour and salt, add chilled water and knead 5 minutes to a firm dough. Rest at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Cook the potatoes
steps.text: Simmer the potatoes about 20 minutes until tender, then peel and crush roughly.

steps.title: Spice the filling
steps.text: Sizzle the cumin seeds, add the ground spices, ginger and chilli, then the potatoes, peas, garam masala and salt. Finish with coriander and lemon and cool.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll 8 rounds, halve them, form cones, fill and seal to make 16 samosas.

steps.title: Blend the chutney
steps.text: Blend the mint, coriander, chilli, lemon, sugar, salt and water.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Fry at 160 °C for 8-10 minutes, turning, until crisp and deep golden. Drain and serve warm.

tips: A firm dough with little water gives crisp, blistered pastry.
Fry low and slow: hot oil browns the outside before it crisps.
Cool the filling completely before shaping so the pastry does not soften.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best fried and eaten the same day. Cool leftovers, refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 2 days, re-crisped in a 200 °C oven for 6-8 minutes until piping hot.
